reason: The text demonstrates agency in multiple non-leader figures. Most significantly, the cry of enslaved Israel (צַעֲקַת בְּנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּאָה אֵלָי - 'the cry of the sons of Israel has come to me') moves God to action, showing that the enslaved people exercise consequential agency despite lacking official leadership. Additionally, Jethro (a non-leader relative) exercises agency in granting Moses permission to depart. Moses himself exercises agency even before becoming a leader—he turns aside to observe the burning bush. The narrative structure shows non-leaders' voices and actions as causally significant to the unfolding of events.
